Made by... D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by... D.I. Crawford

S. I Report of 28.3.40
on the subject f-

Extensive enquiries have been made by
detectives to discover the office or communication
address of the Shanghai Municipality Boyscouts
Committee but without success.
Following the arrest of Chao Wei-tsao
( 趙慶祖 ), leader of the local Chinese boyscout,
by the Japanese Gendarmerie in conjunction with the
Shanghai Municipal Police, from his home at No.3,
Lane 183, Taku Road, on November 23, 1939,—because
of a refusal to incorporate his organization with
the Wang Ching Wei administration,—the affaire of
the boyscouts committee were for a short period
left to the care of Loo Lih ( 羅力 ), former Secretary,
who it is reported has gone over to the Wang Ching
Wei Clique and consequently there is no responsible
officer at present taking care of the affaire of
the organization.

FILE

Kuh Pao hwa
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

侦探们进行了广泛调查，试图查明上海市政厅童子军委员会的办公地点或通讯地址，但未获成功。
1939年11月23日，本地中国童子军领袖赵庆祖（Chao Wei-tsao）因拒绝将其组织并入汪精卫政权，被日本宪兵队会同上海公共租界工部局警务处从其大沽路183弄3号的家中逮捕。此后，童子军委员会的事务在短期内交由前秘书罗力（Loo Lih）负责。据报，罗力已投靠汪精卫派系，因此目前该组织事务并无负责人照管。

of the Chinese Boy Scouts War Time Service Corps with office

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The following is a translation of the sketches on
the placard found outside the Boy Scout Headquarters at
178 Tientsin Road on October 11 by Central Station and
brought to Special Branch the same day :
(1) Front sheet, bearing the characters "The War of
Resistance of the Popular Mass, October 10th Special
Issue, Cartoons," "Prepared by the Propaganda Section
of the Chinese Boy Scouts War Time Service Group."
(2) Sketch showing the erection of a red "Double Cross"
(meaning October 10 anniversary) bearing the national
emblem of China.
(3) Sketch of two pictures showing :-
(a) A Japanese female (supposed to be weeping) and her
child sitting by the seaside and a red "Double
Cross" at the other side of the sea, marked,
"While the Sun and the Moon shine all over the
world, happiness does not follow suit."
(b) A Chinese celebrating the October 10 anniversary
despite the fact that he has a wound on his head,
the wound being marked "the Four Eastern Provinces."
(4) Sketch of General Chiang Kai Shek and the march of
Chinese soldiers, marked "Let the whole nation unite
under the guidance of General Chiang and drive away
the Japanese imperialists !" "Poison gas is
not so dreadful as we have imagined. We can be
prepared against it."
(5) Short essay entitled "Letter to countrymen on the
occasion of the National Day," stating that the nation
has awakened under the oppression of the imperialists

Subject Seizure of quantity of shovels on North Soochow Road by Boy Scouts.
Made by Det. Gibson. Forwarded to

Sir,

At 6.45 p.m. 18/9/37 ... (Central) brought to the
station a complainant, Mr. T. H. Ming (周志醒), proprietor
of the E. C. Comr'l & Ind. Co., 681 Peking Rd., who reported
that a quantity of shovels had been seized on North Soochow
Road by Boy Scouts.

The complainant stated that on the 17/9/37 he arranged for
the supply of 420 shovels to the International Industrial
Corporation, Continent Bank Building, 713 Nanking Road,
(a British concern registered in Hong-Kong). About 10.0
... 18/9/37 the shovels were sent to the Aylmer Neo Jetty
on Soochow Creek for delivery to the buyer but before
the goods were handed over a party of Boy Scouts accompanied
by officials of the Shanghai Refugees Relief Association
arrived on the scene and alleged that the shovels were being
supplied for use by Japanese. 312 shovels which were lying on
the jetty were then loaded into a boat and taken to 745
Soochow Road. The complainant's assistant, who was in charge
of the consignment, was then instructed to report to the
complainant that enquiries would be made regarding the destina-
tion of the goods.

Detectives visited 745 Soochow Road which was found to
be the evacuating office of the Shanghai Refugees Relief
Association of the Footman Guild. The seized property was found
in a boat moored to a jetty outside the office.

Tsang Koh Chong (张启昌), the official in charge of the
office admitted that the shovels had been seized. He was
brought to the station for enquiries.

据本团一名成员报告，昨日下午5时许，浦东同乡会米市场内，一名米店店主与一名司机因车费纠纷发生斗殴，引来大量人群围观，随即697号童子军介入并劝散人群。人群中有一名身材矮小瘦削的男子，自称是侦探，并猛烈推开该童子军。当被问及是否有名片或携带委任证时，该男子袭击了童子军，击打其胸部。“这不关你的事，”袭击者说道。鉴于其无任何身份证明且行为如此暴力，受害者试图将其带至二楼办公室。行至中途，袭击者再次企图施暴，此时另一名童子军赶到现场，协助将其带至二楼。在办公室里，

man claiming himself to be a detective produced
a pistol and pointed it at the boy scout, which

man fast in his arms. All the men in the office
resented and insisted that the assailant should
withdraw his pistol. Seeing that he could not
offend so many people, he put back his pistol in

severely punished. On the other hand due considera-

Suspect released following arrest by scout.

D. I. Biddy

Sir,

At 7.50 a.m. on 8/9/37, C.P.C. 1384 and Boy Scout 1721, named Tsai Bei Yuen (蔡桂元), attached to "Wei Feeng" Girls School on Avenue Road, brought to this station one named Hou Zang Kwai (花長奎), age 60, Tungchow, N.F.A., who was apprehended on Tonquin Road near Markham Road by the Boy Scout on suspicion of being a traitor. Both went to the Red Cross Society on Sinza Road where they were seen by C.P.C. 1384 who brought them to this station.

Questioned the Boy Scout stated that he suspected Hou Zang Kwai of being a traitor because of the presence of a small circle scratched upon his head. This proved to be two straight scratches about 1" in length upon the suspect's head. Questioned, at length, no evidence could be obtained which would substantiate the suspicions of the Boy Scout.

A bayonet type of knife was found in the possession of the Boy Scout. This was considered to be a very dangerous weapon in the hands of one who is engaged in such activities and, on the instructions of the D.D.C. "B" area was confiscated. C.I. were informed and D.S.I. Bradley attended and removed all parties to Crime Branch Headquarters for questioning.

Following interrogation at C.I. suspect was released at 12noon 8/9/37 and the Boy Scout cautioned in the presence of his Chief Scout.

Copy to Special Branch.

嫌疑人经童子军逮捕后被释放。

督察 Biddy

先生，

1937年9月8日上午7时50分，C.P.C. 1384 和隶属于爱文义路 (Avenue Road) “维风”女校的编号1721童子军蔡桂元 (Tsai Bei Yuen)，将一名名叫花长奎 (Hou Zang Kwai)、60岁、江北通州人的男子带至本捕房。该男子是此前由该童子军在通肯路 (Tonquin Road) 靠近马克姆路 (Markham Road) 附近因涉嫌充当汉奸而逮捕的。两人先去了新闸路的红十字会，被 C.P.C. 1384 看见，随后将其带至本捕房。

经讯问，该童子军称他怀疑花长奎是汉奸，因为其头上有一个刻划的小圆圈。经查实，那是嫌疑人头上两道长约1英寸的直线划痕。经详细讯问，未能获得任何证据来证实该童子军的怀疑。

在该童子军身上发现一把刺刀式刀具。鉴于从事此类活动的人持有此种武器被视为极其危险，根据“B”区副总监的指示，该刀具被没收。已通知刑事调查处 (C.I.)，副巡官 Bradley 到场并将所有相关人员带往刑事处总部进行讯问。

经刑事调查处讯问后，嫌疑人于1937年9月8日中午12时被释放，并在其童子军团长面前对该童子军予以警告。

副本送特务处。

1937年9月9日。

My name is Mo Loh Juen, aged 27, native of Kiangsu. I am a piece goods merchant and at present residing at No. 19 An Li, off Nuling Road.

At 2.30 p.m. on the 1/9/37, I received a telephone message from Mo Loh Ming's family reporting that Mo Loh Ming and Chiang S Ling had both been arrested by Boy Scouts and Plainclothes men attached to the Guard Section of the City Relief Committee Association and that they were at that time detained at the Postung Build.

On strength of this information, I immediately attended the scene and there, from enquiries being conducted, ascertained that the above 2 persons were accused by fellow countrymen of having profiteered by selling boat tickets to refugees.

Being one of the committees of the Provisional of Relief Camp of the Yangtze Guild, I vouched for their honesty but this was not regarded as true and in consequence I myself was also detained and instructed to sign a statement confirming the non-sale of the alleged boat-tickets.

We three were subsequently taken to the S.M.P.S. under the escort of representatives of the Guard Section, City Relief Committee Association, where we were detained until 1.30 p.m. 4/9/37, when we were ordered to be released on shop security.

My motive in making this report at your Station is similar to that made by Mo Loh Ling.

The above is my true statement.

Signed.

经华探 172 号和本人询问，查明如下：

1937 年 9 月 3 日上午 11:25 左右，小贩陈阿二正在招待一名顾客，背对着一个中型炉灶，炉灶顶部有一个大铁锅，里面正在煮一些土豆。当小贩转身时，他看到嫌疑人正在重新盖上锅盖，因此立即怀疑正在烹饪的蔬菜被人动过手脚，嫌疑人立即被几名因骚乱而被吸引到现场的旁观者抓住并拘留。

With reference to the attached news article
appearing in the Social Evening News dated August 30 regarding
the discovery on August 29 of six traitors among refugees
housed in camps, enquiries made at the "Disaster Relief
Federation of Shanghai Benevolent Societies", 35 Yunnan Road,
show that the newspaper information is barely untrue.

On August 31, three refugees arrived from Yangtzepoo
and were accommodated in the Dah Kwan (大莞) Refugee Camp,
472 Foochow Road, (Louza District). Later it was suspected
that they were traitors, through being found in possession of
badges and cheques written in the Japanese language. These
three suspects were at 9 p.m. removed from the camp by a party
of Chinese boy scouts to the "Disaster Relief Federation of
Shanghai Benevolent Societies", which supports this camp,
situated in the Jen Chi Tang (仁济堂) premises, 35 Yunnan
Road (Louza District), where they were detained until 10 a.m.
September 1. Mr. Ying Kwan-te (殷冠之), Chief of the
"Guard Section" (警值组) of the Refugee Relief Committee
of the Disaster Relief Federation of Shanghai Benevolent
Societies, who is concurrently Chief of the Relief Section of
the 2nd Department of the Shanghai City Government Police
Bureau, then had the suspects brought before him. Following
investigations made by him, the suspects were ordered to be
released owing to lack of evidence. In conversation,
Mr. Ying passed the remark that the suspects were bound with
ropes when they appeared before him.

Questioned as to which boy scouts were concerned in
the case, Mr. Ying stated that they belonged to the War Time
Service Group of the Shanghai Municipality Boy Scouts!

Yesterday 2,282 refugees were repatriated to

The Wukiang Fellow Countrymen's Association has
established a Relief Committee at House No.31 Dong Chung
Fong (同春坊), Burkill Road. 140 refugees were
repatriated to their native place yesterday by the Committee
in question.

to leave Shanghai for their respective native places.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by [Signature]

A new organization styled the "War Time Service
Group of the Shanghai Municipality Boy Scouts' Committee"
has been established in the Wei Foong (渭風) Girls'
school, Lane 138, 22 Tatung Road. Mr. Hsu Kuo-dz
(徐國茲), Chief of the 50th Chinese Boy Scouts Corps with
headquarters in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building,
North Soochow Road, is in charge of the Service Group. The
Group claims to have a total of 1,600 Chinese boy scouts at
its disposal. The chief work of the Group is as follows : -
1) To maintain order in refugee camps.
2) To escort wounded soldiers and maintain order in hospitals
for wounded soldiers.
3) To propagate general precautions for public protection
during war time.
4) To take suspected traitors mobbed on streets, to the
Police or to the office of the Service Group, to be
properly dealt with.

In connection with the last mentioned item, it is
learned that between August 13 and 29, about twenty suspected
Chinese traitors were taken, instead of to the Municipal Police
or the French Police, to the office of the Service Group from
various places. On completion of investigations made
by the office of the Service Group, all were either released
or escorted to their respective homes.
